title: From Blind Spots to Merged PRs: Continuous Agentic Performance Optimization - May Walter, Hud
talk_summary: A CTO describes an autonomous weekly agentic workflow that mines production runtime data (function-level traces via MCP), scores high-ROI performance opportunities, verifies fixes by re-running tests, and surfaces a small human-readable report instead of a flood of PRs. The core lessons are grounding agents in real runtime evidence, encoding senior-engineer playbooks as skills, and gating autonomous output on high-confidence verification before human review.

takeaways.technique: Verify fixes by re-running tests and measuring runtime impact before surfacing
takeaways.what_they_do: The agent doesn't just propose a fix; it applies it, reruns tests, and measures the impact on the specific production flow, so the human receives a verified result rather than a plausible suggestion.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the agent actually fixes it reruns the tests and sees the impact that it had on that specific flow

takeaways.technique: Prod-to-code: function-level runtime context, not service-level metrics
takeaways.what_they_do: They capture context at the function/file level (where agents reason) and link it to the endpoint/cron/consumer that triggered it, capturing forensic detail only when a request exceeds a P99 threshold.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the agent's context lies on a function and file level, not on an service and endpoint level

takeaways.technique: Encode senior-engineer playbooks as reusable skills over a query layer
takeaways.what_they_do: On top of a query language they add a set of skills (e.g. trace an HTTP 500 to its origin, diff a memory spike against baseline) so agents follow a consistent method instead of re-deriving queries each run.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the skills actually help work with that data so that agents can use it

takeaways.technique: Score opportunities by ROI (impact x risk) and surface one at a time
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of opening 80 PRs, they rank by hot-path frequency, business criticality, and risk, then surface a single human-readable gist to build appetite and habit.
takeaways.evidence_quote: no one wants to wake up for, you know, a rain of 80 pull requests
takeaways.numbers: 80 pull requests (example of what they avoided)

takeaways.technique: Guardrails and scoring as the reliability layer for autonomous runs
takeaways.what_they_do: They treat scoring and guardrails as what makes automation trustworthy, and note autonomous workflows need ~80-90% confidence before handing to a human, unlike in-IDE use.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the scoring and the guardrails are what makes this reliable

takeaways.technique: Vendor-neutral workflow infra with scheduled + webhook triggers
takeaways.what_they_do: They built workflows to be neutral across compute, harness, and model, with scheduled runs and webhook triggers (e.g. on SLO breach), so they can swap models as things change.
takeaways.evidence_quote: vendor neutral in terms of compute and where it runs, in terms of the harness and in also in terms of the model
